History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
26-year-old woman presents with 3-day history of new-onset dry, pruritic, erythematous rash on hands and arms beginning after swimming; impression of irritant/contact dermatitis. Treated with topical steroid, emollient, and OTC antihistamine; advised follow-up if no improvement within one week.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Dry, itchy skin on hands and arms.  
• Onset/progression: Began a few days ago, noticed after swimming; persistent.  
• Character: Dryness, pruritus, redness; denies pustules, vesicles, cracking, discharge, bleeding, fever, or sweating.  
• Associated symptoms: Feels tired; denies vomiting, diarrhea, urinary symptoms, appetite change.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: Coconut butter applied for several days without benefit; stress at work noted.  
• Systems review:  
  ‑ Constitutional: Tiredness; no fever.  
  ‑ GI: No nausea, vomiting, diarrhea; good appetite.  
  ‑ GU: Normal urination.  
  ‑ Respiratory/Cardiac/Neuro: Not discussed.  
  ‑ Dermatologic: See above; no prior eczema/dermatitis.  
  ‑ Other negatives: No sweating, no spots.

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• No prior dermatologic disease.

Medications:
• Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Coconut butter (topical moisturizer, OTC).  
Allergies:
• Possible lactose intolerance (food intolerance); no drug allergies documented.

Social History:
• Occupation: Primary school teacher; reports increased work stress and long hours.  
• Living situation: Lives alone.  
• Tobacco: Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol: Does not drink alcohol.  
• Recreational drugs: Denies use.

Family History:
• Father – asthma.  
• Mother – hay fever.  
• No known family history of skin disease.

Physical Examination:
• Not performed during teleconsult.

Investigations:
• None ordered or reviewed.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected contact/irritant dermatitis of hands and arms  
  ‑ Plan:  
    • Provide patient information leaflet on dermatitis.  
    • Prescribe topical corticosteroid cream (specific product/dose not documented).  
    • Recommend liberal use of emollients throughout the day.  
    • Advise OTC oral antihistamines (e.g., chlorphenamine/Piriton or loratadine) for pruritus.  
    • Avoid known irritants; monitor skin after swimming; continue stress-reduction strategies.  
    • Follow-up: If no improvement within 7 days, return for re-evaluation.

General plan items:  
• No need for analgesics at present.  
• Encourage adequate hydration, skin care, and stress management.

Quality checks:

• Missing but expected elements: Vitals, detailed physical examination, full drug allergy list, dosage for Microgynon and prescribed steroid.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear overall; occasional minor inaudible words but core clinical details intact.
